speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of the current talent shortage in Singapore's financial sector (a) how does the Ministry ensure that efforts to attract foreign talent are balanced with the development and progression of the local workforce in the financial sector; (b) what measures are in place to maintain such balance in this sector; and (c) how does the Ministry monitor their effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This balanced approach has been key to Singapore’s success as a global financial centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: At pre-entry and entry levels, MAS provides funding for internships, apprenticeships and job rotation programmes to equip our polytechnic and university students and fresh graduates with the skills to take on the jobs that we have created in the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: At the mid-career level, MAS provides opportunities for finance professionals to both upskill and reskill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We work with training providers to develop relevant courses, subsidise these course fees and develop career conversion programmes with financial institutions for our mid-careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: At the senior-level, MAS supports the development of senior leaders through overseas postings, leadership programmes and by building leadership networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Financial institutions also recognise the importance of growing and developing local talent to meet their manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For instance, in 2024, I had the opportunity to work with OCBC to launch “OCBC Ignite”, an accelerated career programme that comprises an internship and apprenticeship on full-time employment with the bank.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: UBS also partnered the Government to develop the UBS-SUPER programme in 2020 and has trained over 400 fresh graduates and mid-career professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: UBS has also doubled the number of Singaporeans sent on overseas postings, compared to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, would you like to round up your answer?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We regularly engage senior management of key financial institutions on their workforce needs and composition and on how we can work with them to develop local talent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: COMPASS also recognises and gives additional weight to global talent who bring in skills in shortage, while the Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) attracts and anchors top global talent from around the world.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: By maintaining this balance, we will attract more investments and provide good jobs, career choices and progression opportunities for our locals.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
